# `frontend/src/lib/api-client/` — generated TypeScript clients

**DO NOT EDIT FILES IN THIS FOLDER MANUALLY.**

Per [ADR 0022](../../../../docs/adr/0022-nswag-pipeline.md), the four
`*.v1.ts` files in this folder are generated by NSwag from each backend
host's `/openapi/v1.json`. Manual edits will be reverted by the next
generation, and a pre-commit hook (added in T-0016) rejects diffs that
touch generated files without a matching `.spec-hashes.json` update.

## Files

| File | Source | Host |
|---|---|---|
| `customer-api.v1.ts` | `http://localhost:5001/openapi/v1.json` | `Makables.Web.Customer` |
| `maker-api.v1.ts` | `http://localhost:5002/openapi/v1.json` | `Makables.Web.Maker` |
| `admin-api.v1.ts` | `http://localhost:5003/openapi/v1.json` | `Makables.Web.Admin` |
| `public-api.v1.ts` | `http://localhost:5004/openapi/v1.json` | `Makables.Web.Public` |

## How to regenerate

1. Start the backend hosts you want to regenerate against:
   ```bash
   cd backend/src
   dotnet run --project Makables.Web.Customer  # in one terminal
   dotnet run --project Makables.Web.Maker     # in another
   # ... etc.
   ```
2. From `/frontend/`:
   ```bash
   npm run generate:api
   ```
3. Commit the regenerated files together with the matching
   `.spec-hashes.json` update.

## Why hand-written helpers are not allowed here

A consumer that needs to wrap a generated client (e.g. attach auth headers,
parse errors into the `Result<T, ApiError>` shape from `lib/runtime/`)
should live in `frontend/src/lib/api-client-helpers/` — a sibling folder
that is **not** auto-generated.

## Why generated files are committed

The frontend's CI is the consumer of these files; running NSwag in CI
would require starting the .NET backend, which is too heavy for a
frontend-only build. Committing them moves the cost to the developer
making the contract change, and the pre-commit hook + CI parity check
keep drift from accumulating.
